title: Normalized dualizing complexes at finite residue-field coefficients
statement:
Let $k$ be any field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, and let $A$ be a finite field of characteristic $\ell$. Let $a:T	o s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism of a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small etale sites use bounded complexes with constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], the derived tensor and internal Hom [def-kun-derived-tensor, def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and compact support $Ra_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Let $a^!$ be the right adjoint of $Ra_!$ on these constructible categories (equivalently, the constructible restriction of the bounded-below exceptional adjoint), and put $\Omega_{T,A}=a^!A_s$.

This adjoint exists, $\Omega_{T,A}$ is bounded constructible, and $H_A(-,\Omega_{T,A})=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\Omega_{T,A})$ preserves bounded constructibility. For every bounded constructible $P$ the evaluation-defined map
$$P\longrightarrow H_A(H_A(P,\Omega_{T,A}),\Omega_{T,A})$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $P$. The normalization is the dimension function $\delta_T(t)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(t)$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field], with coefficient unit $A_s$ on $s$. Let $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For bounded constructible $P,Q$ the evaluation-defined comparison $
u_T^*H_A(P,Q)	o H_A(
u_T^*P,
u_T^*Q)$ is an isomorphism. Consequently, after setting $\Omega^{\mathrm{pro}}_{T,A}=
u_T^*\Omega_{T,A}$, the same duality, evaluation and biduality assertions hold on the pro-etale bounded category whose cohomology sheaves are constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] (equivalently, the etale-origin category [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]), with the actual ambient pro-etale internal Hom. No separable-closedness, perfectness, or finite cohomological dimension of $k$ is required.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 2.4.4.1, Proposition 4.1.2 (finite-type extraordinary pullback of normalized potential dualizing complexes), Theorems 5.1.1, 6.1.1 and 7.1.3; finite exceptional existence also Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.7.18; etale/pro-etale Hom comparison Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.3.16

proof.text: By [lem-exc-fields-excellent], $k$ is excellent. On each affine finite-type $k$-chart of $T$, [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] shows that its coordinate ring is excellent and in particular Noetherian. Thus $T$ and $s$ are Noetherian excellent and $\ell$ is invertible on both. The structure map is compactifiable by [thm-nagata-compactification]. Apply [lem-per-finite-exceptional-preservation], first with $B=\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$ and then with $B=A$. It supplies $Ra_{!,B}\dashv a_B^!$ on the bounded-below etale categories, preservation of bounded constructibility by both functors, and hence their restriction to the full bounded constructible categories. This proves the stated adjoint existence without asserting finite global Galois cohomological dimension.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.18 and Theorem 6.7.1; excellence hypotheses checked using Stacks Tags 07QW and 07QU

proof.text: On $s$ take $\delta_s=0$ and the degree-zero unit $\Lambda_s$. The definition [def-per-potential-dualizing] makes this a pinned potential complex directly: the local scheme at the only point is $s$, support there is all of $s$, and $R\Gamma_s\Lambda_s=\Lambda_s$ with its identity pinning on the residue-field site. There are no codimension-one specializations on $s$, so the compatibility equation has no instances. This works also when $k$ is imperfect or has infinite $\ell$-cohomological dimension: supported cohomology here is a complex on $s_{\mathrm{et}}$, not its derived global Galois invariants.

source.place: Expose XVII, Definition 2.1.2 applied to the zero-dimensional base

proof.text:
Apply [lem-per-potential-extraordinary-pullback] to $a$ and this pinned unit. It gives $K= a_\Lambda^!\Lambda_s$ with potential pinnings for
$$\delta_T(t)=\delta_s(a(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(a(t))}\kappa(t)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(t).$$
Every hypothesis was checked in step 1; the base pinning is step 2. This fixes the relative dimension normalization, including for non-equidimensional $T$; no absolute dimension function or perfection of $k$ has been substituted.

The finite-extension clause of [lem-per-finite-exceptional-preservation], with $B=\Lambda$, $C=A$, $L=\Lambda_s$, gives the counit-normalized isomorphism
$$u:A_T\otimes^L_\Lambda K\xrightarrow{\sim}a_A^!A_s=\Omega_{T,A}.$$
Apply [lem-per-potential-local-duality] to the potential complex $K$ from step 3. It proves bounded constructibility of the source of $u$, preservation of $D^b_c$ by its internal-Hom dual, and evaluation biduality for every bounded constructible $A$-complex. These assertions transfer through $u$ to the actual $\Omega_{T,A}$. Explicitly postcomposition with $u$ identifies the two dual functors, evaluation becomes $u\circ\mathrm{ev}$, and transposing that same equality twice identifies the two bidual maps. Thus the isomorphism obtained is the evaluation-defined map in the statement, natural in $P$. The extended pinnings of step 3 give exactly the stated normalization; at $T=s$ the identity compactification and identity adjunction give $\Omega_{s,A}=A_s$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Theorems 6.1.1 and 7.1.3; finite free adjoint comparison as in Bhatt–Scholze 6.7.18

proof.text:
We prove the Hom comparison, rather than treating a constructible sheaf as site-perfect on all of $T$. Work first over an affine open $V\subset T$. Let $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ be an affine ind-etale basis object over $V$, with $U_i/V$ affine etale finitely presented; these objects form a basis by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. For any integer $n$, put $C=H_A(P,Q)$, which is bounded below since $P$ is bounded above and $Q$ bounded below. The sections clause of [lem-per-ind-etale-derived-hom-continuity] identifies
$$H^n R\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{proet}},\nu_V^*C)=\varinjlim_i H^nR\Gamma((U_i)_{\mathrm{et}},C|_{U_i}).$$
By internal-Hom restriction and the global-Hom identity [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction, lem-pur-rhom-global-sections], each term on the right is $\operatorname{Hom}_{D((U_i)_{\mathrm{et}},A)}(P|_{U_i},Q|_{U_i}[n])$. The Hom clause of [lem-per-ind-etale-derived-hom-continuity] identifies their colimit with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)}(P|_U,Q|_U[n])$. The target has the required common lower bound because ordinary etale pullback is exact; over a field the constructible first variable has perfect finite-dimensional values, as required by that lemma.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 6.3.16, via Lemma 6.3.14 and Remark 6.3.2

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], restriction of $
u_V^*P$ and $
u_V^*Q$ to $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is respectively $
u_U^*(P|_U)$ and $
u_U^*(Q|_U)$. Full faithfulness of $
u_U^*$ on $D^+$ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], followed by the global-Hom identity and restriction [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], identifies the last Hom group in step 5 with
$$H^nR\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{proet}},H_A(
u_V^*P,
u_V^*Q)|_U).$$
All arrows in these two steps are induced by pullback of morphisms. Under the tensor-Hom transpose their action is pullback of evaluation. Thus their composite is precisely the map on $H^nR\Gamma(U,-)$ of the evaluation-defined comparison [def-sf-evaluation-hom-site-comparison]. This also explains its naturality in both variables. It is an isomorphism for every $n$ and every basis object $U$. Both source and target are bounded below, so [lem-weil-pbc-basis-derived-detection] proves that comparison is invertible on $V$. Since the affine opens cover $T$, locality for covering families [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative](1) proves invertibility on $T$.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.16: compare global Hom groups on every affine pro-etale test and detect the resulting derived isomorphism

proof.text: The intrinsic pro-etale constructible category also equals the etale-origin category here. Indeed [det-pe-constructible-comparison-classical] applies to a constructible $A$-sheaf $F$ because $A$ is Noetherian and $T$ is qcqs: it gives $F\cong\nu_T^*F_0$ for an etale module sheaf $F_0$. On each locally closed stratum, [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies the pullback of the etale restriction of $F_0$ with the given finite locally constant pro-etale restriction of $F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-finite-local-constancy-reflection], the etale restriction is finite locally constant. Thus $F_0$ is constructible. Conversely comparison pullback takes finite constant local models to the same finite constant local models on each stratum. Now let $M$ have intrinsically constructible cohomology in $[a,b]$. For $a=b$, the sheaf assertion gives an etale witness $F_0[-a]$. Inductively the truncation triangle with last term $\mathcal H^b(M)[-b]$ has the other two terms already of etale origin. Full faithfulness on $D^+$ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] lifts its connecting morphism to the etale category. Its cone, shifted once, is bounded constructible, and exact pullback [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] gives a triangle isomorphic to the original triangle; hence it gives an etale witness for $M$. Finite induction proves equality of the two bounded constructible categories. This retains the intrinsic conclusion of the item over arbitrary $k$.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.4 and Section 6.3: classical descent on strata, followed by finite truncation induction

proof.text: By definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], every object of the stated pro-etale constructible category has the form $\nu_T^*P$ with $P\in D^b_c(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. The exactness of comparison pullback [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] preserves its finite cohomological bounds. Set $\Omega^{\mathrm{pro}}=\nu_T^*\Omega$. Apply the comparison just proved first to $(P,\Omega)$ and then to $(H_A(P,\Omega),\Omega)$, whose etale arguments are bounded constructible by step 4. It identifies the actual ambient pro-etale dual and double dual with the pullbacks of the etale dual and double dual. Because the comparison is defined by evaluation, its defining transpose equation identifies the pro-etale evaluation with pulled-back evaluation and, on transposing a second time, the pro-etale bidual map with the pullback of the etale bidual map. The latter is an isomorphism by step 4, hence so is its pullback. This proves all pro-etale assertions for every object, independently of its chosen etale representative. The same argument with morphisms gives naturality. No step uses a separably closed or perfect base or a cohomological-dimension bound for $k$.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.16: evaluation-normalized transport of duality to the finite-coefficient constructible realization
